if it uses wine and open source file formats how is it really different from linux? is it just a gnome/xfce/etc. replacement?

Well, Gnome/xfce .etc are all Desktop Environments, they alter how the system looks, and how you interact with it on the surface, they are an interface, nothing more. ReactOS isn't a DE, it's an entire operating system. It's not linux at all, because it does not use the linux kernal (the central piece of code that determines how the OS interacts with filesystems and hardware and whatnot), it uses a custom kernal built to be very similar to the windows NT kernal in an attempt to make NT programs natively compatible. In a sense, lets say an operating system is a car. the Kernal is the car's chassis: everything is built on top of it, the distribution (in linux's case,things like fedora, debian, arch .etc, in window's case xp/vista/7/8/10) is the engine, its built ontop of the chassis, and all engines that fit on the same chassis have to be pretty similar- a smart car's chassis isn't going to fit the engine of a semitruck, but they don't have to be identical, and then the Desktop Enviornment, along with other programs, is the car's body and color. There's some basic level of intercompatibility here- while I can't put the body of a minivan onto the engine and frame of a smartcar (trying to put the win 7 UI onto fedora, for instance), but I can put a Pickup or an Suvs body on the same frame, because they are pretty similar (putting XFCE onto Fedora, despite the fact that it defaults to Gnome). ReactOS is trying to recreate a Chassis that can fit programs that were designed for windows without altering the programs, despite putting a different engine on, and not being allowed to see the blueprints of the original chassis (windows NT)

it uses a custom kernal built to be very similar to the windows NT kernal in an attempt to make NT programs natively compatible.

But it uses the wine compatibility layer to run those applications, that is where my confusion is. If it is an NT clone then it should run windows code natively, if it can't run programs without wine then how is that different than running linux with wine?

I guess what i'm saying is that if wine ran on beos we wouldn't say that beos was an opensource windows project. so how is this different?

Well, the kernal of an operating system is concerned with interacting with things such as the filesystem, but its very rare that a program is built entirely off this functionality; there are other commands in other parts of the OS that programs rely on, often found in groups called "Libraries," when a program says "Make a new file at this location," it's the kernal that is needed for compatibility, but when the program says "create a new window on top of the others," it relies on commands held in libraries provided by the window manager. What Wine does is it takes command calls that rely on windows- only libraries, and either fakes the response from the library that the program expects, or forwards the commands to the proper linux/ other OS library, after converting it to the equivalent command in the host OS.
TL;DR ReactOS uses a Windows clone kernel and Gnu/Linux uses the Linux kernel.

Because they can't automatically detect social queues to the extent that others can, you have to teach them. This means you need to become more self aware and pass what you feel is easy second nature on to your kid so that she can at least kind of identify those things.
